stage_probability.definition: Unconditional (first stage). P that by end of 2060, in the same year, (i) automated firms hold >= 80% of output with realized automation depth >= 50% in sectors covering >= 50% of 2026 employment, and (ii) economy-wide net labor demand after CES/Baumol reallocation and new tasks is >= 15% below 2026. Headline = equal-weight linear pool of 4 capability views (judgmental prior; draws reweighted to Grace et al 2024 HLMI; to FAOL; to Metaculus AGI), each also weighted for consistency with 2026 exposure. CI = Monte Carlo sampling error only (weighted bootstrap); structural_band = range across alternative model forms and calibration anchors.

timeline.definition: Pooled: calendar year (end of year) of first S1 event among draws with event by 2060

regulation_tax_threshold.note: payroll-parity strength s taxes s/0.3 of gross labor cost saved (0.3 = full parity), non-tradable share, trigger 3% displacement, drawn lag

structural_band.note: Structural variants rescaled to full-sample baseline via paired difference. Toggles of single priors (regulation, ceilings, lags) are NOT in the band; they are prior tails.

for_other_stages.note: End-of-year values, years 2027..2100. Demand feedback (S2) is OFF in the headline; its effect is in scenario 'STRUCT demand feedback on'.

samples.note: 4000 random draws; event_year null if none by 2100.

H50_2026_hours.source: METR (May 2026): best model 50% horizon >=16h, measurements >16h unreliable; Opus 4.6 ~12h. Extrapolation to 2026-09 at 3-7mo doubling, widened for the measurement ceiling [web]

doubling_months.source: METR TH1.1 (Jan 2026): ~7mo long run, ~4.3mo since 2023, ~3-4mo recently [web]

trend_break_mean_years.source: Judgmental; per-draw mean of exponential waiting time to a slowdown (compute/power/data limits)

post_break_slowdown.source: Judgmental: doubling-time multiplier after the break

p_plateau.source: Judgmental (NOT tuned in v2): prob. of near-halt after break (x50 slowdown)

ceiling_decades.source: Per-draw saturation of benchmark 80% horizon, decades above 2026 level (~3h): ~50h to ~300,000h (5-95%). Judgmental; long tasks are decomposable, so the upper range is wide

p_no_transfer.source: Prob. benchmark horizon gains largely fail to transfer to economic tasks (METR limitations note; Humlum & Vestergaard realized savings 3%). In that case economic horizon grows at U(0,0.3) of benchmark rate

p_accel.source: Prob. of AI-R&D feedback: after benchmark 80% horizon passes the threshold, each doubling takes x accel_factor the previous (AI 2027 / METR superexponential discussions). Judgmental

accel_threshold_h.source: Benchmark 80% horizon at which AI R&D is substantially automated (~1 work-month). Judgmental

accel_factor.source: Doubling-time shrink per doubling in acceleration branch

task_horizon_median_h.source: Judgmental; 2026 end-to-end feasibility a few % of tasks (Acemoglu 2024 4.6%; Humlum & Vestergaard 3%)

task_horizon_logsd.source: Judgmental: tasks span minutes to months

mess_scale.source: Draw-level scaling of sector messiness multipliers (METR messiness results)

ceiling_scale.source: Scaling of sector automation ceilings; widened to include x0.7 (IMF 2024: ~half of AE exposure is complementary; Eloundou 2023)

phys_gap_doublings.source: Physical 'horizon' below cognitive in 2026, log2 units (McKinsey 2025: 13% robot-automatable hours vs 44% agent). Judgmental

phys_doubling_months.source: Physical capability doubling time; slower than software (hardware iteration, data scarcity). Judgmental

p_plateau_phys.source: Prob. dexterity/generalist robotics stalls (x20 slowdown after its own break, mean 5y). Judgmental

phys_ceiling_decades.source: Physical capability saturation, decades above the 2026 COGNITIVE level (physical starts phys_gap_doublings lower). Judgmental

r_phys_2026.source: Robot all-in cost (capex annualized + maintenance + integration) / wage per replaced task, 2026. IFR/ARK: arm ~$27k (2017) to ~$11k, but integration 2-4x hardware [web]

r_phys_decline.source: e-fold/yr decline of robot cost; IFR ASP -3-5%/yr recently, -80% 1995-2017 (~7%/yr) [web]

r_phys_floor.source: Floor on physical automation cost / wage (materials, energy, maintenance). Judgmental

ai_cost_ratio_2026.source: AI compute cost per feasible task / wage; Epoch price trends [web]

ai_cost_decline.source: e-fold/yr decline of frontier-task cost; sticky frontier pricing (S3)

oversight_cost.source: Verification/oversight cost (wage units) per automated task at full depth; rises linearly with depth (longer tasks need more checking). Judgmental

liability_premium.source: Liability/insurance premium (wage units) for automated tasks, scaled by sector (health x2). Judgmental

deployment_lag_years.source: Realizing feasible tasks (David 1990; Brynjolfsson, Rock, Syverson 2021 J-curve); physical x1.5; speeds up with adopter share (learning by doing)

adoption_cost_multiple.source: One-off integration/intangible cost as multiple of annual savings (intangibles several x technology cost: Brynjolfsson, Rock, Syverson 2021), annualized 5y@10%

firm_het_sigma.source: Log-sd of firm-level net gain (firm heterogeneity; replaces step sigmoid). Judgmental

selection_rate.source: Log-odds share gain per yr per unit price gap (Koch, Manuylov, Smolka 2021; Acemoglu, Lelarge, Restrepo 2020)

switch_rate.source: Max yearly R->A hazard among willing firms (Comin & Hobijn 2010; Fed 2026 worker adoption +31%/yr)

competitive_forcing_prob.source: Research prior #22; psi = 3p multiplies rival-threat term

benevolence_max_sacrifice.source: Max margin a fully benevolent owner forgoes (net margins ~5-10%)

union_strength.source: Cost-equivalent at 100% density (ILA 2024-25; WGA/SAG 2023); x2 in government

human_niche.source: Share of B2C demand paying the premium

gov_budget_pressure.source: Government adoption responds to budget savings at this fraction of a market firm's incentive; no rival threat. Judgmental

sigma_sub.source: CES elasticity of substitution across sectors (<1 = Baumol); Nordhaus 2008 finds stagnant sectors price-inelastic [lit]

phi_recycle.source: Share of real income gains from automation that becomes effective demand (capital-income recycling after monetary/fiscal offset; S2 hook). Judgmental

demand_lag_years.source: Adjustment of sector demand to prices/income. Judgmental

reinstatement_rate.source: New-task labor demand per yr; Acemoglu & Restrepo 2019 JEP: 0.47%/yr 1947-87, 0.35%/yr 1987-2017 [web, verified]

newtask_automatable.source: New tasks automatable in proportion abar * this. Judgmental

wage_floor.source: Reservation wage floor (min wage ~0.3-0.4 of median plus transfers) / 2026 wage. Judgmental

labor_income_demand_share.source: Elasticity of firm demand to aggregate labor income (demand externality for the PD test; B2C-weighted). Judgmental

p_pact_legal.source: Prob. a retention pact is legal/brokered (antitrust normally forbids competitor agreements; government-brokered sector deals possible). Judgmental

discount_factor.source: Annual discount factor for repeated-game sustainability

p_regulation.source: Prob. binding response once displacement bites; robot taxes mostly rejected so far (EU Parl. 2017)

reg_strength.source: Effective strength after capture, 0-0.3 (tax cost share; payroll-parity fraction = strength/0.3; licensing ceiling cut = 2*strength). Beta prior

trade_leak.source: Share of tradable output escaping national regulation

p_gov_veto.source: Prob. a regulating polity also halts public-sector automation (procurement/political veto)

robot_lag_years.source: v1 structural variant only: physical tasks on the cognitive curve shifted by this lag
